reasoning:
I'm checking whether defaulting the start color to the first entry of cubes conflicts with the round 1 episodes—those showed mixed behavior, sometimes starting with the smaller-count color and sometimes the larger, so the arbitrary "larger required count" default doesn't clearly match the pattern either.

For the second proposal, skipping a cube within 40 px of bin center unless it's the last of its color seems like a one-episode observation rather than a broader rule, though it doesn't directly contradict the earlier annotation about detections near bin center. I'll treat it as a modest, tentative clause rather than a committed rule, since it might just reflect the oracle avoiding collision with the bin.

Now I'm drafting the exact quote replacements: updating the empty-`placed` default to specify taking the first needed-color cube in `cubes` not excluded by the bin-proximity clause, and revising the oldest-cube-pick rule to first set aside any cube within about 40 px of the bin center before selecting among the remainder.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: If `placed` is empty, any needed color may be started; as the fixed default, start the needed color with the larger required count, ties to the color named first in the goal instruction.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: If `placed` is empty, any needed color may be started; as the fixed default, start with the color of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) whose color is still needed and which is not set aside by the bin-proximity clause below; at step #1 that is the needed-color cube nearest the bin's center, of whichever needed color it is. Do not choose the start color by required count or by a fixed color preference.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: Among the cubes of that color, pick the oldest one on the table: point at the position of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) that has that color.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: Among the cubes of that color, first set aside every cube whose remembered or detected position lies within about 40 px of the bin center, as long as some other cube of that color lies farther from the bin (a near-bin cube is picked only when it is the last cube of its color on the table). Among the cubes that remain, pick the oldest one on the table: point at the position of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) that has that color and is not set aside.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: The age order in `cubes` is the only criterion among same-colored cubes:
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: After the bin-proximity set-aside, the age order in `cubes` is the only criterion among same-colored cubes:

revision.refused: The per-step replacements for the same-color selection (nearest the current gripper, farthest from the bin, smallest y, last entry of the list) stay out, as in rounds 1 to 3: the report checked each against the four blue picks of the episode and the single-color episodes and found each contradicted, while the age order fits every single-color episode. The residual order among the blue cubes that were all 58 to 61 px from the bin is not given a new criterion; age order remains the default there. The start-color change is committed only as a replacement default: round 1 established that no rule derived from the goal (larger count, smaller count, fixed color) explains which color is started, and the larger-count default has now failed in this episode, so the default is moved to the first needed entry of `cubes`, which coincides with the step #1 tie-break already committed in round 2 rather than adding a second one. The 40 px set-aside is committed as a reach rule, not as a redefinition of what counts as a cube: the 10 px bin-center exclusion and the 20 px table-cube threshold in the `cubes` field from round 3 are unchanged, so the near-bin cube is still entered and carried in memory and is picked when it is the last of its color. Neither memory document changes, since the policy's memory matched the annotation at every failing step.
